chunks: What al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Safwan, from Sa'id ibn Yasar, who said:

I said to Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام: We buy sheep in Mina, and we do not know whether they have been taken to 'Arafah or not. So he said: They do not lie; there is no problem upon you; offer it as the sacrifice.

key_terms.الْغَنَمَ: sheep intended for purchase as sacrificial animals
key_terms.بِمِنًى: at Mina, the location where the sacrificial rite is performed during hajj
key_terms.ضَحِّ: offer the animal as the sacrifice
key_terms.عُرِّفَ: was identified or taken through the required process connected to the rite
key_terms.لَا يَكْذِبُونَ: they do not lie; a basis for trusting the sellers' report

ai.seo_question: Can a person offer a sheep bought in Mina as a sacrifice if he is unsure whether it was properly identified?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about purchasing sacrificial sheep in Mina when one is unsure whether the animal has met the required condition of having been brought for identification. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام permits reliance on the sellers' apparent honesty and allows the sacrifice to be offered.
